fact.box: SOXL (Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF), US-listed
fact.claim: SOXL's lowest close of 2025 was $8.22, on April 8, 2025, and it closed at $66.68 on November 4, 2026. So $10,000 held from that low would have been worth about $81,000, roughly $71,000 more than someone who sold at the low, before fees, taxes and currency. This is a 3x daily leveraged fund. It fell about 11% in premarket on November 5, and one intraday quote showed it down about 34%, so the figure moves fast in both directions and past results do not promise future ones.

why.line: SOXL owns no chip company outright. It's a bet on the 30 biggest US chip stocks, at three times the daily move.
why.line2: It aims for 300% of the index's move each day, then starts over.
why.means: Because SOXL resets every day, it can climb fast when chip stocks rise, as it did from the 2025 low, and fall just as hard, like the roughly 34% intraday drop seen this week. That means the fear is not always a discount: holding it for months can end far from three times the index's return in either direction.
